Week 2 Part 5 VERIFY (1): naive versus cells force paths

Working directory: week2/
Command: cargo test --manifest-path md/Cargo.toml --test force_paths -- --nocapture --test-threads=1
Source of deterministic fixtures and printed values: md/tests/force_paths.rs
Force units: Lennard-Jones reduced units; shifted potential, rc = 2.5; minimum-image periodic boundaries.
Each detailed row gives one atom position, both two-component force vectors, and componentwise absolute differences.
Maximum force difference is max over every atom and both components; potential difference is absolute.
Acceptance tolerances: force <= 1e-10 * max(1, max |F_naive component|);
potential <= 1e-10 * max(1, |E_pot,naive|).

Interpretation and uncertainty
The observed global maxima are max |delta F_component| = 0.00000000000000000e+00 and max |delta E_pot| = 0.00000000000000000e+00.
Both paths use the same pair formula. The cell path sorts candidate atom indices, so these fixtures
traverse interacting pairs in the same order as the naive path; zero observed differences are
therefore plausible. Agreement between paths is not an independent check of the Lennard-Jones
formula. Different compiler, platform, or summation order could produce rounding differences,
which the stated scale-aware tolerances allow.
The shifted potential is continuous at rc, but the force is not shifted. The below/at/above rc
cases compare paths on the SAME coordinates in each case; they do not require force continuity
as the separation crosses rc. These fixed configurations do not cover every possible state.
